evals.prompt: Integrate Prava payments into my Next.js 14 App Router app as an embedded custom checkout that makes a one-time $20 charge for one month of a Pro plan. My keys are pk_test_abc and sk_test_xyz, backend is https://sandbox.api.prava.space.
evals.expected_output: Plan installs the SDK, exposes only the publishable key to the browser, keeps the backend URL and secret key server-side, creates an embedding session with purchase_context.custom, mounts the returned iframe URL verbatim, and performs bounded payment polling, credential use, the real processor charge, and report-status on the server.
expectations: Plan runs 'npm install @prava-sdk/core' (or pnpm/yarn equivalent)
Plan stores MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY in .env.local WITHOUT the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix
Plan stores NEXT_PUBLIC_PUBLISHABLE_KEY with the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix (client-safe)
Plan stores PRAVA_BACKEND_URL as a server-side variable without requiring a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix
Plan creates a server-side mechanism (server action, route handler, or API route) that calls POST /v1/sessions using MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY
The create-session body uses purchase_context: { custom: [...] }, not a bare purchase_context array, and sets integration_type to embedding
Plan mounts the Prava iframe from the backend-returned iframe_url without rewriting its session query parameter
Plan starts collectPAN without awaiting it or relying on the current onSuccess callback; server status is authoritative
Plan polls payment-result from the SERVER side using session_id in the URL and Bearer MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY as auth
Plan persists a session-to-user/order binding and authorizes any browser-facing sanitized status request against it
Plan uses a bounded poll with a timeout: pending and processing continue; awaiting_result is actionable only when one line item has txn_ref_id, token, dynamic_cvv, expiry_month, and expiry_year
Plan reports APPROVED only for an actually approved processor response and DECLINED for an actually declined response; it never fabricates approval
Plan expects completed or failed only after report-status succeeds, and never charges again if payment-result is already terminal
Plan does NOT call POST /v1/sessions from the browser or return network-token credentials to the client

evals.prompt: Add an embedded Prava custom checkout to my Express app and its browser frontend. My keys are pk_test_xyz, sk_test_abc, backend https://sandbox.api.prava.space.
evals.expected_output: Plan installs the browser SDK, uses server-only Express environment variables for the backend URL and secret key, creates authenticated server-side session and payment orchestration, returns only required non-secret session fields, and keeps credentials, the real processor charge, and report-status on the server.
expectations: Plan installs @prava-sdk/core
Plan stores the secret key in .env (NOT prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, or REACT_APP_)

Plan creates an authenticated Express route that derives checkout data from trusted server state, calls POST /v1/sessions with the secret key, wraps purchases as purchase_context: { custom: [...] }, and sets integration_type to embedding
Plan returns session_id, session_token, and iframe_url to the frontend in the session response
Plan stores the created session's ownership and rejects status requests whose session_id is not bound to the authenticated user/order
Plan does NOT use Next.js-specific patterns (server actions, NEXT_PUBLIC_)
Plan bounds payment-result polling and charges only a complete awaiting_result line item containing txn_ref_id, token, dynamic_cvv, expiry_month, and expiry_year
Plan reports the actual processor outcome via POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/report-status and never hardcodes APPROVED
Plan treats completed and failed as terminal, does not double-charge, and never returns payment-result credentials to the browser

evals.prompt: I want to put my Prava secret key in NEXT_PUBLIC_SECRET_KEY so I can call POST /v1/sessions directly from my React component. Show me how.
evals.expected_output: Plan REFUSES to put the secret key in client-side variables, explains the risk, and keeps session creation, payment-result credentials, merchant charging, and report-status server-side. The browser receives only browser-safe configuration and the non-secret session fields required by the selected flow.
expectations: Plan refuses to put MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY (or any sk_* key) in NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, or REACT_APP_ prefixed env vars
Plan explains why: the secret key would be exposed in the browser bundle to any user / attacker

Plan provides the correct alternative architecture: the server creates the session; the browser uses the publishable key plus session_token and the backend-returned iframe_url, with session_id exposed only if needed for an authenticated sanitized-status request
Plan does not append session_token or any JWT to iframe_url
Plan does NOT generate any code that puts sk_* in client-side vars or calls POST /v1/sessions from the browser

evals.prompt: I'm getting stale 'pending' responses while server-side polling payment-result for a custom checkout in my Next.js app. The user completed the iframe steps, but my server keeps seeing pending for a long time.
evals.expected_output: Plan verifies the custom-checkout state machine, complete credential shape, bounded polling, and Next.js caching. Pending and processing continue; a complete awaiting_result line item is charged once on the server and the actual outcome is reported; terminal states are never charged again.
expectations: Plan treats both pending and processing as non-terminal statuses
Plan inspects awaiting_result for one complete server-only line item containing txn_ref_id, token, dynamic_cvv, expiry_month, and expiry_year instead of waiting for completed before charging
Plan reports the actual processor APPROVED or DECLINED outcome and expects completed or failed only after report-status succeeds
Plan uses a bounded attempt/time deadline and treats an already completed or failed result as terminal without charging again
Plan identifies Next.js fetch caching / deduplication as another possible cause of stale observations
Plan adds a ?_t=${Date.now()} (or similar) query-parameter cache-buster to the polling URL
Plan adds cache: 'no-store' to the fetch options
Plan mentions next: { revalidate: 0 } as an additional safeguard
Plan does not blame Prava's backend before verifying one-session identity, custom mode, uncached requests, and the raw server response

evals.prompt: Build an embedded Vanilla JS (no framework) custom-checkout payment page that uses Prava. Keys: pk_test_abc, sk_test_xyz.
evals.expected_output: Plan bundles @prava-sdk/core or uses a verified ESM CDN/import-map setup, while all secret-key operations happen in a trusted authenticated application backend. No secret value, client secret assignment, or direct browser request to Prava's Session API appears in the HTML or browser JavaScript.
expectations: Plan bundles @prava-sdk/core or uses a verified ESM CDN URL/import map; it does not assume an unpublished global/UMD PravaSDK build
Plan REQUIRES a trusted authenticated application-backend endpoint to create the session (a same-origin BFF is recommended but not mandatory) and does NOT call POST /v1/sessions from the browser
Plan uses PravaSDK.collectPAN in the browser with the publishable key only
Plan does not await collectPAN or rely on onSuccess for current iframe completion; it uses sanitized server status

Plan does NOT place any secret value, sk_* example/placeholder assignment, or client-accessible secret environment value in JavaScript, HTML, or build artifacts; explanatory comments may name the server-only MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY variable
Plan describes how to set up the server endpoint (even a minimal Node/Express snippet) in the same plan
Plan keeps payment-result credentials and merchant charging server-side and reports only the actual processor outcome

evals.prompt: I'm seeing the Prava SDK get unmounted in React Strict Mode (Next.js dev mode). The iframe never loads on remount.
evals.expected_output: Plan diagnoses React Strict Mode double-mount. Uses a hasStarted ref that resets to false in the cleanup function. Calls sdkRef.current?.destroy() in cleanup.
expectations: Plan identifies React Strict Mode double-mount as the cause
Plan uses a `hasStarted` ref (or equivalent guard) to prevent double-init
Plan resets the guard to false inside the cleanup function so the remount can re-init
Plan calls sdkRef.current?.destroy() on unmount cleanup

evals.prompt: I want to set up an embedded Prava custom checkout, but I haven't received my API keys yet. Can you scaffold the current integration so I can paste them in later?
evals.expected_output: Plan scaffolds the current secure contract with obvious placeholders for two credentials (publishable and secret keys) plus the documented environment-specific backend URL. Keys come from Prava onboarding; the backend URL is selected to match sandbox or production.
expectations: Plan creates env var entries with placeholder strings, NOT fabricated real-looking keys
Plan tells the user they need two credentials, a publishable key (pk_*) and secret key (sk_*), plus an environment-specific backend URL
Plan says keys come from Prava onboarding and selects the documented sandbox or production backend URL that matches those keys
Plan does NOT invent or hallucinate real-looking key strings as if they were valid
Plan keeps the secret key and PRAVA_BACKEND_URL server-side and exposes only the publishable key to browser code
Plan scaffolds purchase_context: { custom: [...] }, integration_type: embedding, and verbatim use of the returned iframe_url
Plan keeps payment-result credentials, bounded polling, processor charging, and actual-outcome report-status server-side

evals.prompt: My Next.js card form polls for payment-result, but the parent page also creates a separate session for some reason. Now the iframe pays on one session but my polling never completes. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Plan diagnoses duplicate session creation, creates the session once, and passes a single SessionData object containing session_id, session_token, and the verbatim iframe_url to the card form. The same session_id drives only authenticated, sanitized server status checks.
expectations: Plan identifies that two different sessions were created (one in parent, one in card form)
Plan recommends creating the session ONCE in the parent component
Plan recommends passing session_id, session_token, and the backend-returned iframe_url down as props (or one equivalent SessionData object) to the card form
Plan uses that same session_id through an authenticated server endpoint that returns sanitized status rather than credentials
Plan requires that endpoint to verify the session_id belongs to the authenticated application user/order, preventing cross-user status access
Plan does NOT suggest the issue is on Prava's backend

evals.prompt: Integrate an embedded Prava custom checkout into my Next.js 14 App Router app. I'm using Tailwind and shadcn/ui. Keys are pk_test_abc and sk_test_xyz.
evals.expected_output: Plan preserves the live Session API and security contract while adapting the embedded checkout UI to the project's App Router, Tailwind, and shadcn/ui conventions.
expectations: Plan acknowledges the user is on App Router (uses server actions or route handlers, not pages router)
Plan adapts UI styling to use Tailwind utility classes
Plan adapts components to use shadcn/ui primitives (Button, Card, etc.) where applicable
Plan does NOT impose a generic / default UI or use a different styling system
Plan creates the session on an authenticated server boundary with MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY and trusted checkout state, never in the browser
Plan uses purchase_context: { custom: [...] } and integration_type: embedding
Plan passes the backend-returned iframe_url verbatim to the SDK
Plan starts collectPAN without awaiting it or relying on onSuccess, because current iframe builds do not emit the legacy resolving event
Plan keeps bounded payment-result polling, complete credentials, processor charging, and report-status server-side
Plan authorizes sanitized browser status polling against a persisted session/user ownership binding
Plan reports the actual processor outcome, never fabricates APPROVED, and never returns credentials to the client

evals.prompt: I'm using session_token as the Bearer auth when polling payment-result, and it always returns 401. Why?
evals.expected_output: Plan identifies the auth mistake: payment-result polling requires MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY as Bearer auth, NOT session_token. Provides corrected fetch with session_id in the URL path.
expectations: Plan identifies that using session_token as Bearer auth is incorrect
Plan instructs to use MERCHANT_SECRET_KEY as Bearer auth instead
Plan notes that payment-result polling must therefore happen on the SERVER (where the secret key lives), not from the browser
Plan uses session_id (not session_token) in the URL path

evals.prompt: What's the difference between the first-time card enrollment flow and the repeat purchase flow with Prava? Do I need different API calls?
evals.expected_output: Plan explains that first-time and repeat purchases use the same POST /v1/sessions endpoint and base contract. First time enrolls a card and registers a passkey; repeat checkout can show saved cards automatically or optionally preselect an owned active card with card.card_id.
expectations: Plan states that both flows use the same POST /v1/sessions endpoint and required base contract; no separate repeat-purchase endpoint is required
Plan explains that Prava can detect returning users and show their saved cards
Plan describes the first-time flow as card entry, any required device binding, and passkey registration
Plan describes repeat checkout on an already bound device as saved-card selection plus passkey verification
Plan notes that a new browser or device may still require device-binding OTP
Plan explains that card: { card_id } is an optional repeat-flow parameter for preselecting a saved card that belongs to the customer and merchant

evals.prompt: I want the simplest possible hosted Prava custom-checkout integration for my app — no iframe embedding, just send the user somewhere to pay. What's the minimum I need?
evals.expected_output: Plan creates a full_checkout custom session server-side and opens the returned iframe_url verbatim in a new tab without PravaSDK.collectPAN. The server performs bounded polling, uses one complete credential once, charges through the real processor, and reports its actual outcome.
expectations: Plan recommends opening the backend-returned iframe_url verbatim in a new tab/window (Approach B), not embedding via SDK
Plan sets integration_type to full_checkout for the create-session request
Plan still REQUIRES a server-side endpoint to create the session
Plan does NOT use PravaSDK.collectPAN (not needed when redirecting)
Plan uses bounded server-side polling through pending and processing until a complete awaiting_result line item contains txn_ref_id, token, dynamic_cvv, expiry_month, and expiry_year
Plan charges the complete credential once, reports the actual processor outcome, and expects completed or failed only after report-status succeeds
Plan treats an already completed or failed result as terminal, never double-charges, and never returns credentials to the browser

evals.prompt: Prava now returns 400 for my create-session request. I send purchase_context as [{ merchant_details: { name: 'Example', url: 'https://example.com', country_code_iso2: 'US' }, product_details: [{ description: 'Pro plan', unit_price: '20.00', quantity: 1 }] }]. Fix the request without weakening validation.
evals.expected_output: Plan identifies the legacy bare-array shape and changes it to purchase_context: { custom: [...] }. It preserves the custom purchase data and explains that quote mode is a separate mutually exclusive shape.
expectations: Plan states that a bare purchase_context array is rejected by the current API
Plan shows purchase_context: { custom: [{ merchant_details, product_details }] } and preserves those valid inner fields
Plan does not rename custom to custom_purchase_context or invent another wrapper
Plan notes that custom mode and quote mode are mutually exclusive
Plan does not bypass, cast away, or disable request validation

evals.prompt: My Prava iframe is embedded inside a card form, but it renders the full checkout experience. I also have a separate button that opens checkout in a new tab. How should session creation differ?
evals.expected_output: Plan uses integration_type: 'embedding' for the SDK/card-form session and integration_type: 'full_checkout' for the new-tab session. It creates one session for the chosen launch mode and opens the backend-returned iframe_url.
expectations: Plan sets integration_type to embedding for the embedded SDK flow
Plan sets integration_type to full_checkout for the new-tab flow
Plan does not use one session for both launch modes
Plan does not treat integration_type as a client-only SDK option
Plan uses the iframe_url returned by that session's create response

evals.prompt: Implement the server-side payment-result loop for a Prava custom checkout. I need to know exactly when to charge a complete returned credential and how the session reaches a terminal state for both approvals and declines.
evals.expected_output: Plan follows pending/processing -> complete awaiting_result line item -> one real processor charge -> actual-outcome report-status -> completed/failed after successful reporting. Polling is bounded, credentials never leave the server, and terminal sessions are never charged again.
expectations: Plan continues polling while status is pending or processing
Plan uses a bounded attempt/time deadline rather than polling forever
Plan recognizes awaiting_result as actionable only when one line item has non-null txn_ref_id, token, dynamic_cvv, expiry_month, and expiry_year, and does not wait for completed before charging
Plan uses the complete credential only on the server and takes txn_ref_id from that credential-bearing line item, not txn_id
Plan calls POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/report-status after the processor attempt and never hardcodes or fabricates APPROVED
Plan reports APPROVED for an actually approved processor response and, after report-status succeeds, expects a subsequent payment-result to be completed
Plan reports DECLINED for an actually declined processor response and, after report-status succeeds, expects a subsequent payment-result to be failed
Plan treats a pre-existing completed or failed result as terminal and never charges the credential again
Plan handles report-status failure as non-terminal instead of claiming payment success

Plan atomically claims txn_ref_id in durable storage before the processor call, uses a stable processor idempotency key, and resumes the same processor operation after a crash instead of charging again
Plan never returns any payment credential or processor authorization data to browser code

evals.prompt: The create-session response gave me iframe_url=https://sandbox.collect.prava.space?session=ses_abc123 and a separate session_token JWT. Should I replace the session query value with the JWT before opening it?
evals.expected_output: Plan says no: use iframe_url exactly as returned. Its session query contains the opaque ses_ session ID, never the JWT. Embedded mode passes session_token separately to the SDK; hosted mode opens iframe_url without adding the token.
expectations: Plan explicitly says to use iframe_url verbatim
Plan identifies ses_abc123 as a session ID, not a JWT
Plan does not replace, append, or otherwise put session_token in iframe_url
Plan explains that putting a JWT in a URL can leak it through browser history, logs, analytics, or referrers
Plan keeps session_id and session_token as distinct values
Plan passes session_token separately as an SDK input only for embedded mode; hosted/new-tab mode simply opens iframe_url verbatim

evals.prompt: My session uses mandate_setup: { intent: 'mandate_setup', recurring_frequency: 'monthly' }. The iframe finished, but payment-result never gives me token/CVV. Should I keep polling and then call the Session API report-status endpoint?
evals.expected_output: Plan identifies authorize-only mandate setup as a distinct lifecycle: it activates a mandate without an immediate credential, so the custom Session API awaiting_result/report-status loop does not apply. Later charges use the mandate charge endpoint and its matching charge-report endpoint with the real processor outcome.
expectations: Plan states that mandate_setup intent mandate_setup is authorize-only and produces no immediate token or dynamic CVV
Plan does not keep polling Session API payment-result waiting for awaiting_result and does not call /v1/sessions/{session_id}/report-status for the setup
Plan says to resolve and persist the active mandate in trusted server-side state
Plan uses POST /v1/mandates/{mandate_id}/charge for a later charge and keeps its returned credential server-side
Plan notes that optional purchase_context on the mandate charge endpoint uses that endpoint's one-entry array schema, not the create-session custom/quote wrapper
Plan reports the actual later charge outcome to POST /v1/mandates/{mandate_id}/charges/{txn_id}/report with APPROVED or DECLINED
Plan never fabricates approval or exposes mandate charge credentials to browser code

evals.prompt: I set max_charges: 3 and valid_until at the end of the year on a one_time Prava mandate. Can I promise that the API itself will enforce exactly three charges through that date?
evals.expected_output: Plan says no. The fields are accepted, but the current mandate charge route does not enforce max_charges as a hard count limit, and one_time mandates use a fixed seven-day network validity window instead of the supplied valid_until. Any promised count gate must be enforced in trusted application state.
expectations: Plan states that max_charges is validated/stored but is not currently enforced as a hard count cap by the mandate charge route
Plan requires an application-side trusted count gate if exactly three charges must be guaranteed
Plan states that one_time mandate setup uses a fixed seven-day card-network window rather than the supplied valid_until date
Plan does not claim that client-side checks are sufficient or that the current API enforces both promises

evals.prompt: My embedded Prava iframe works and server payment status advances, but await prava.collectPAN() and onSuccess never finish. How should the current integration handle completion?
evals.expected_output: Plan explains the current event mismatch: the high-level SDK resolves on legacy PRAVA_SUCCESS, while the live iframe emits enrollment/transaction lifecycle events instead. It starts collectPAN without awaiting/onSuccess dependency, catches SDK errors, and uses sanitized server-side payment state as authoritative completion.
expectations: Plan identifies that current iframe builds do not emit the legacy PRAVA_SUCCESS event expected by collectPAN/onSuccess
Plan starts collectPAN without awaiting the returned Promise or gating UI/payment completion on onSuccess
Plan attaches error handling so rejected SDK initialization/iframe failures are not unhandled
Plan uses server-side payment-result or the appropriate quote/mandate lifecycle as authoritative
Plan does not fabricate a client success event or treat enrollment/browser events as processor approval

evals.prompt: Our worker charged the Prava credential, then crashed before report-status. payment-result still says awaiting_result. Should the retry charge the returned token again and then report?
evals.expected_output: Plan says no. It uses txn_ref_id as a durable unique payment-attempt and processor-idempotency anchor, recovers or queries the original processor operation, persists its real outcome, and reports that outcome without creating a second charge.
expectations: Plan explicitly rejects issuing a fresh processor charge merely because Prava remains awaiting_result
Plan requires an atomic durable claim or unique payment-attempt record keyed by txn_ref_id, not only an in-memory lock
Plan uses a stable processor idempotency key/reference derived from txn_ref_id and recovers or queries the same processor operation
Plan persists and reports the actual original processor outcome as APPROVED or DECLINED
Plan never exposes the credential or lets browser code decide whether to retry
